title: Få til or klare å — managing to do something
goal: Distinguish successful completion from ability or effort.

objectives.statement: Distinguish successful completion from ability or effort.

sections.title: A difficult morning at the community centre

spans.value: Mina works at a community centre in Bergen. She and Jonas are preparing an information meeting for new volunteers. Ten minutes before the meeting, the projector stops working.
Projektoren virker ikke. Jeg får ikke til å vise presentasjonen.

blocks.translation: The projector isn’t working. I can’t manage to display the presentation.

spans.value: Har du prøvd den andre kabelen?

blocks.translation: Have you tried the other cable?

spans.value: Ja, men jeg får det fortsatt ikke til.

blocks.translation: Yes, but I still can’t get it to work.

spans.value: La meg se. Jeg klarte å bruke projektoren i går, men den var vanskelig å starte.

blocks.translation: Let me see. I managed to use the projector yesterday, but it was difficult to start.

spans.value: Vi har bare ti minutter. Klarer du å ordne det før møtet?

blocks.translation: We only have ten minutes. Can you manage to fix it before the meeting?

spans.value: Jeg skal prøve. Der! Nå fikk jeg det til.

blocks.translation: I’ll try. There! Now I got it to work.

spans.value: Flott! Da klarer vi å begynne i tide.

blocks.translation: Great! Then we’ll manage to start on time.

sections.title: Focusing on the result with få til

spans.value: when the important point is that something works, succeeds, or reaches a successful result. It is especially common when a task has been difficult, has required several attempts, or has previously failed.

Read short situations about practical problems, such as opening a document, connecting a printer, or preparing a room. Identify which sentence reports that the task eventually worked. Then explain briefly what result was achieved. ## Focusing on ability or effort with klare å {#focusing-on-ability-or-effort-with-klare-aa role=model objectives=obj-faa-til-or-klare-aa-01}
when the focus is on whether a person can cope with a task or has enough ability, strength, time, concentration, or determination to do it.

no.value: Klarer du å bære denne esken?

en.value: Can you manage to carry this box?

spans.value: The question is about the person’s capacity. The box may be heavy, awkward, or difficult to carry.

no.value: Jeg klarer å lese teksten uten ordbok.

en.value: I am able to read the text without a dictionary.

no.value: Hun klarte å holde seg våken under hele møtet.

en.value: She managed to stay awake during the entire meeting.

spans.value: This reports success, but the wording highlights her effort or endurance.

no.value: Vi klarte ikke å bli ferdige før klokka fem.

en.value: We didn’t manage to finish before five o’clock.

spans.value: The group did not have enough time or did not overcome the difficulty.

no.value: Han klarer å forklare problemet.

en.value: He is able to explain the problem.

no.value: Han klarte å forklare problemet.

en.value: He managed to explain the problem.

spans.value: can describe current ability or ask whether a task is possible. The past form
often reports that someone overcame a challenge.

sections.title: Checkpoint: connect the task to the person

spans.value: Work with short descriptions of people under pressure: someone is tired, has little time, carries something heavy, or must concentrate in a noisy room. Complete each description with a natural statement using
with an infinitive and make the difficulty or effort relevant to the person. ## The central contrast {#central-contrast role=contrast objectives=obj-faa-til-or-klare-aa-01}
The two expressions overlap. Both can describe success, and both may be translated as manage to. The best choice depends on how the speaker views the situation.

no.value: Endelig fikk jeg til å installere programmet.

en.value: I finally succeeded in installing the program.

spans.value: The installation is now working. The result is central.

no.value: Jeg klarte å installere programmet selv om instruksjonene var uklare.

en.value: I managed to install the program even though the instructions were unclear.

spans.value: The speaker presents the installation as something they were able to accomplish despite difficulty.

no.value: Vi fikk til en god middag med det vi hadde i kjøleskapet.

en.value: We succeeded in making a good dinner with what we had in the refrigerator.

spans.value: The successful dinner is the focus.

no.value: Vi klarte å lage middag før gjestene kom.

en.value: We managed to make dinner before the guests arrived.

spans.value: The focus is on completing the action within a difficult time limit.

no.value: Teknikeren fikk til lyden etter flere forsøk.

en.value: The technician got the sound working after several attempts.

no.value: Teknikeren klarte å finne feilen på fem minutter.

en.value: The technician managed to find the fault in five minutes.

spans.value: The technician’s ability and achievement under time pressure are prominent.

spans.value: This is a difference in perspective, not an absolute division. In some situations, either expression is possible, but the emphasis changes.

no.value: Hun fikk til å løse oppgaven.

en.value: She succeeded in solving the task.

spans.value: This draws attention to the successful solution.

no.value: Hun klarte å løse oppgaven.

en.value: She managed to solve the task.

spans.value: This draws attention to her accomplishment or ability.

The meeting has started, but Mina and Jonas face one more problem.

sections.title: Integrated practice: solve the meeting problems

spans.value: Continue Mina and Jonas’s meeting with several short exchanges. Include a new practical problem, an attempt to solve it, a question about whether one person can cope with a difficult action, and a final successful result.
Use both target patterns, but keep their perspectives distinct. Your response should use
for something that eventually works or succeeds. ## Final retrieval and review {#final-retrieval-and-review role=recap objectives=obj-faa-til-or-klare-aa-01}
Without looking back, write two short Norwegian sentences about a new situation. In the first, use
to emphasize someone’s ability or effort. In the second, use
to emphasize a successful result. Briefly identify the difference in focus in Norwegian.

prompt.value: Mina byttet kabel og fikk vist presentasjonen. Hvilken forklaring passer best til de to setningene?

explanation.value: Begge uttrykkene kan fortelle at Mina lyktes. «Fikk til» framhever resultatet av å få presentasjonen til å virke; «klarte å» framhever Minas evne eller innsats. Samtalen viser at hun lyktes, men gjør ikke ett uttrykk feil.

options.text: Both sentences report success; fikk til foregrounds the successful result, while klarte å foregrounds Mina’s ability or effort.
options.why: The cable change explains the achieved result; the alternate wording can still truthfully describe Mina's success while focusing on what she managed to do.

options.text: Fikk til reports success, while klarte å only reports an unsuccessful attempt.
options.why: Klarte å can describe successful completion too; it foregrounds capacity or effort rather than denying the result.

options.text: Both sentences report success and necessarily emphasize the same thing.
options.why: The result of the task and Mina's ability or effort are different possible points of focus.

options.text: Only the first sentence can be used because Mina has already shown the presentation.
options.why: The second sentence is also grammatical and compatible with the stated success.

prompt.value: Skriv en melding til søsteren din om hagearbeidet. Tomatfrøene begynte å spire etter at du flyttet pottene til vinduet. Du var usikker på om du rakk å plante dem ut før ferien, men fikk det gjort. Bruk både «få til» og «klare å».

payload.judge_prompt: Check criteria message-purpose, uses-target-expressions, supplied-facts, target-patterns, and focus-distinction. Require a form from the få til family to foreground the successful result of getting the seeds to sprout, and a form from the klare å family to foreground the writer's effort or ability to plant them before the holiday. Accept natural variants. Both expressions can be natural for either event in other contexts, but a response that reverses or erases the requested result and effort distinction does not meet this task.

criteria.instruction: The response is a message to the writer's sister about the garden work.
The response uses both få til and klare å to describe getting the seeds to sprout and planting them before the holiday.
The response remains consistent with the supplied gardening facts and does not invent a conflicting account.
Uses a natural få til pattern, including få + noun or pronoun + til å + infinitive, for the seeds sprouting, and uses klare å + infinitive for planting them before the holiday.

The sentence about the seeds foregrounds the successful result of sprouting; the sentence about planting foregrounds the writer's effort or capacity to finish before the holiday. Do not pass a response that reverses these requested perspectives or uses both sentences to foreground only the result or only the effort.
Observation only: note which expression is used for each event; the requested result and effort perspectives are the gating focus.
